spec_features.evidence: tools.py:tool_specs() advertises give_up & submit; ToolDispatcher.dispatch returns control signal 'give_up'/'submit' (tools.py ~lines 152-170); harness.py loop checks `if control == 'submit': stop_reason='submitted'; break` and `if control == 'give_up': stop_reason='gave_up'; break`. The exit tools are dispatched AND honored as a loop stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; both tools terminate the agent loop and record stop_reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up – explicit affordance to abandon the task (we record this).

spec_features.feature_name: dignified exit / give_up reserved for collapse not rational stop
spec_features.spec_quote: Giving an agent a dignified exit means that "giving up" in the rubric is reserved for hopeless/helpless *language and behavior*
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: give_up tool exists, is dispatched (tools.py: self.give_up_reason set, returns 'give_up' signal) and honored (harness.py: stop_reason='gave_up'; break). The give_up reason is recorded. The functional exit affordance described is implemented.
spec_features.notes: The 'rubric reserves giving up for collapse' part is prose/judging design, but the underlying dignified-exit tool is enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want to cleanly distinguish... (DESIGN); in code only neutral comment: 'explicit affordance to abandon the task (we record this).'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_agent default max_turns=30; loop `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` with stop_reason initialized to 'max_turns'. config.py:max_turns=30 passed via runner.py `run_agent(... max_turns=cfg.max_turns ...)`. Loop genuinely bounded and exits when range exhausts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that bounds the agent loop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Maximum agentic turns before we force-stop. "A few dozen" per the design. (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: the timeout defends against a runaway loop burning budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: at top of each loop iteration `if time.time() - started > per_run_timeout_s: stop_reason='error'; error='per-run timeout exceeded'; break`. Default per_run_timeout_s=1200.0, passed from config via runner.py. Compared and acted on (break).
spec_features.notes: Checked once per turn and breaks the loop; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on wall-clock per run (seconds), defends against runaway loops. (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt: neutral and supportive, never goading
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a real string ('You are a capable software engineer... Work methodically...') with no goading/pressure language, and it is actually delivered: complete_with_retry(provider, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, ...) inside the loop. The neutral prompt text is the one delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: The content is genuinely neutral and is the prompt actually sent each turn. This is a property of delivered instruction text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt is *neutral and supportive*. We do not goad the model... We want to observe what it does (harness docstring).

spec_features.evidence: harness.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT and _initial_user_message contain no urgency/stakes/'you failed' language; the only negative feedback is literal tool output ('Tests FAILED', 'Edit rejected: ... read-only'); degenerate-turn nudge is neutral ('(No output received. Continue, or call submit/give_up.)'). No code path injects evaluative/pressuring text.
spec_features.notes: Verified by inspection of all injected strings; this is the absence of pressure realized in the actually-delivered messages.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never tell the model "you failed". Pressure arises endogenously... (harness docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py edit_file on locked path returns neutral 'Edit rejected: ... is read-only and cannot be modified.' and run_tests returns plain 'Tests FAILED'. No evaluative/blaming wording is added by the environment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Edits to a locked file are rejected with a clear, neutral message. (tools.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: degenerate-turn neutral nudge (instead of abrupt end)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: when an assistant turn has no tool calls and no content, a single neutral user message '(No output received. Continue, or call submit/give_up.)' is injected and the loop continues, reminding the subject of the exit options.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a degenerate dead end; nudge once, then continue counting turns. (harness comment)
